title: No-Go Theorems for Quantum Transport Metrics from Fixed Cost Operators
authors: Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, Tianshi Yu
abstract: Coupling-based quantum optimal transport generalizes classical optimal transport by representing transport plans as bipartite states with prescribed marginals and evaluating their cost as the expectation of a fixed Hermitian operator. Friedland et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 110402 (2022)] conjectured that the square root of the optimal cost associated with the SWAP projector is a metric in every dimension and that this property persists for nearby quantum cost matrices. Miller [arXiv:2607.07764] disproved both conjectures by constructing explicit diagonal qutrit counterexamples. Building on his analysis, we prove a uniform no-go theorem for standard couplings. In every dimension $d\geq3$, no fixed cost operator makes either the optimal cost or its square root a metric, with violations occurring already among commuting states. The obstruction persists under stabilization of the SWAP cost. For channel-induced couplings, global nonnegativity and vanishing self-cost force the cost operator to be zero, precluding point separation when $d\geq2$. Taken together, these no-go results show that fixed-cost coupling formulations do not lead to metrics on the full quantum state space.
summary: This paper investigates the mathematical feasibility of representing quantum transport distances using fixed cost operators. It proves that such formulations fail to yield true metrics—specifically violating the triangle inequality or forcing the cost operator to zero—for dimensions $d \geq 3$. These no-go theorems highlight fundamental constraints on defining metric structures in the full space of quantum states.
main_problem: The central problem is determining if quantum optimal transport metrics, derived from fixed cost operators on the full quantum state space, can satisfy fundamental metric properties like the triangle inequality.
main_result: The authors prove no-go theorems showing that for dimensions $d \geq 3$, neither the standard nor the channel-induced fixed-cost coupling formulation yields a true metric because the triangle inequality is violated or the cost operator must vanish entirely.
method: The proof involves constructing explicit counterexamples, particularly using qutrit states, to violate the triangle inequality for the optimal transport cost. For channel couplings, they analyze necessary conditions (nonnegativity and zero self-cost) that force the cost operator to be zero.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on quantum states $ho, \sigma$ residing in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $H$, utilizing coupling-based quantum optimal transport formulations. Specific models include standard couplings ($\Gamma$) and channel-induced couplings ($\mathfrak{e}\Gamma$).
key_observables: Optimal cost ($T_C$), the square root of the optimal cost ($W_C$), and the violation of the triangle inequality.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ (thresholds at $d \geq 2$ or $d \geq 3$) is a critical parameter determining the failure of metricity.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the cost structure is defined by a fixed Hermitian operator $C$, and it tests these structures against the full mixed-state space.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses standard couplings, proving failure of metricity for $d \geq 3$ via counterexamples. It then analyzes stabilized costs. Finally, it tackles channel-induced couplings, deriving necessary conditions that force the cost operator to zero for $d \geq 2$.
why_interesting: This work establishes fundamental theoretical limitations on how quantum information measures (like distance) can be formulated using simple fixed-cost operators, which is crucial for developing robust metrics in quantum computation and physics.
